quote_original: Tonight I want you to think of Christ as a cosmic being who contains everyone within him.
context_after: Having died for all, this one being is in all, and will rise in all. Only one being can rise, for only one being fell. One being, containing all within him, fell into this world of death to become individualized as you, as me. That same being will rise in us all, individually: and when he does the divine name “Lord” will be conferred upon the individual in whom he rose.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from You Are A Cosmic Being (1969-05-02).

quote_original: In Paul’s wonderful letter to the Corinthians, he tells us: “From now on I regard no one from the human point of view; even though I once regarded Christ from a human point of view, I regard him thus no longer.” Why?

context_after: Because Paul was led from tradition to self-discovery.
